must.claim: Lines 49 (new): "Once the system has 10 finished buildings, half the time it tries to upgrade a random building instead. If that building can't be upgraded, it does nothing that cycle. If none can be upgraded, it builds."
must.problem: The last two sentences read as describing the same condition (nothing upgradable) but assert opposite outcomes ("does nothing" vs. "it builds"), which is self-contradictory to a reader. It's also not what the code does: the Upgrade branch is always paired with build_random as a select fallback (behavior_tree.json nodes b7c9ed2c-44c2.../0482fbe3-3959... put `Upgrade` and `build_random(biome)` as siblings in a select, and lib/game/system_ai/actions.ex:181-195 upgrade_random/0 returns :fail when no upgradable tile exists). So whenever nothing is upgradable, the system falls straight through to try building in the same cycle — it never 'does nothing' for that reason alone. "Does nothing that cycle" only happens if building also fails, which these two sentences don't distinguish. This is new text in this revision (the prior version just said "half the time it tries an upgrade first," with no failure-mode claim), so it's a clarity/accuracy regression introduced while expanding the page, not a pre-existing issue.
must.fix: Replace the two sentences with one accurate statement of the actual fallback, e.g.: "If nothing can be upgraded, it builds instead." Drop the "does nothing that cycle" claim unless it is independently verified against build_random's own failure case (Helper.get_random_building returning nil) and stated as a distinct, later condition, not as the direct result of a failed upgrade.

must.claim: The revised third bullet under "What it does" reads: "Higher stability makes a Siderian's {ui:galaxy.system.actions.encourage_hate} or [[dominions|Control]] more likely to fail. Stability below 0 counts as 0 here, so it does not make either action easier."
must.problem: The second sentence is cryptic and a player would likely misread it. "Here" has no clear grammatical antecedent (it means "in the Siderian's success-chance roll", never stated), and "does not make either action easier" is a double negative whose implicit subject (easier *for the Siderian*) is never named — the first sentence frames things from the defender's point of view ("more likely to fail"), then the second silently switches to the attacker's point of view ("easier") without saying so. This is also a rule 4 violation ("Point instead of half-explaining"): instead of stating the fact and linking out, the sentence half-explains the underlying max(stability, 0) mechanic that the guide map assigns to the Siderians/dominions pages (docs/help-review/systems/guide-map-rest.md line 419: "Stability defends against Control, max(stability, 0) | Siderians (future)"), and the guide map's planned bullet for this page was simply "It defends the system against a Siderian's Control. See [[dominions]]." (same file, line 452) — a single clean statement plus a link, not an inline explanation of the floor-at-0 rule.

must.problem: Every credit Lex in the code is empire-level. No Lex adds a percentage to a system's credit: all credit-percentage Lexes are `from: :player_credit, to: :player_credit` (doctrine-slow.ex, e.g. credit_perc_1 at :471, +10 %). The player takes in each system's whole credit, Mobility bonus included, as a flat add (player.ex extract_bonus, `from: :direct ... to: :player_credit`). That flat add runs before the player's credit percentage. Run with Core.Bonus (tmp/help-review/system-outputs-acc-r1-len-player.exs): a system making 130 credits (100 + 30 Mobility bonus) with the +10 % credit Lex gives 143 empire credit, not 140. So a real credit Lex does count the Mobility credits. The page's 140 only holds for a system-level credit percentage. The only one in the game is the Erased 'mafioso' skill, +5 % (character.ex:90, `from: :sys_credit, to: :sys_credit, type: :mul`). tmp/help-review/system-outputs-acc-r1-len-stack.exs, case E, confirms the 140 for that kind of bonus.

must.problem: Rule 4 says: "Point instead of half-explaining: 'See [[housing]].' beats a clause that summarizes housing." These two new appositive clauses do exactly the half-explaining the rule forbids: they restate, inline, the fact that administrative-operations.md itself owns as its first OWNS item ("Liberate turns your system into your dominion" / "Administer turns your dominion back into a system", per docs/help-review/systems/guide-map-rest.md). Before this revision the bullets were the correct, rule-4-compliant form: "Administer (see [[administrative-operations]])" and "Liberate (see [[administrative-operations]])" — plain pointers with no summary clause. This revision reintroduces the duplication the rule exists to prevent, and now the fact lives on two pages that could drift out of sync.
must.fix: Revert both bullets to a bare pointer, matching the pre-diff wording and the rest of the page's style: "- Administer (see [[administrative-operations]])" and "- Liberate (see [[administrative-operations]])".
